What the age of Chicago Heights houses means for lead paint

The honest answer for a 1950s-era house in Chicago Heights is probably yes, there is older paint under there, and paint that old can contain lead. What follows from that is method, not a refusal: sheeting, sealed doorways, dust kept where it is made, and a cleanup Chicago Heights homeowners should expect to see done properly.

The practical content of it is dust. Where paint in a Chicago Heights room gets disturbed past about six square feet, twenty outside, or wherever a window comes out, the work has to be contained and cleaned to a standard. That is time at both ends of the job, and it is why an honest quote on 5,816 homes worth of 1958-median housing reads longer than a fast one.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Chicago Heights.

The Census publishes a pre-1980 bucket rather than a pre-1978 one, and on that measure 86.1 percent of the housing sits on the older side of the line in Chicago Heights. Anything built before 1978 sits inside the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule the moment work disturbs its paint. Illinois never took the program on, so the agency behind it here is EPA itself.

None of that is a reason to leave a Chicago Heights house unpainted. It is a reason to know what the setup looks like before anyone opens a sander, and to hear it from the person doing the work rather than from a website.

Questions

Asked about Chicago Heights

What changes the price most on a house here?

Condition, not size. On 1958-median stock in Chicago Heights what varies is how much has to come off or be made good before anything goes on: loose paint, failed caulk, damaged trim, ceilings that have been patched before. Two houses on the same street can differ by a lot on that alone.

Does the lead-safe rule apply to my house in Chicago Heights?

Probably, and the honest answer is that your build year decides it rather than the town. 86.1 percent of housing units in Chicago Heights went up before 1980, so most addresses here land on the pre-1978 side of the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule. It applies to work that disturbs paint, at roughly six square feet per room inside or twenty square feet outside, and to any window replacement. Check the year on your own address and ask whoever quotes you how they handle it.

My house in Chicago Heights is plaster, not drywall. Is that a problem?

It is not a problem, it is a different repair. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so the fix has to address the movement rather than the line. With a 1958 median build year most of Chicago Heights is plaster over lath on at least some walls and ceilings. Say so when you call, because it changes the time estimate and it is better said before the quote than after.

Do you actually come out to Chicago Heights, or is this just a page?

It is 18.2 straight-line miles from the shop in Bridgeview, so it is a genuine drive and the answer depends on the job. A full exterior or a whole interior is worth the trip.
